newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court confirms validity of EU agreement with India.
newsitem.headline: Court confirms validity of EU agreement with India.

text.p: The European Court of Justice confirmed on Tuesday the validity of an agreement designed to promote cooperation between India and the European Union and said its objective was to establish a framework for cooperation.

Portugal challenged the legal basis on which the Council of the European Union concluded the Cooperation Agreement on Partnership and Development between the EU and India, arguing the Council incorrectly relied on treaty provisions which permit qualified majority voting.
Portugal argued adoption of the agreement required unanimous voting because it deals with issues of human rights, energy, tourism, culture, drug abuse control and intellectual property.

The court found the Council has specific competence to conclude agreements with non-member countries in the sphere of development cooperation. The court said the agreement determined areas for cooperation, but did not "prescribe in concrete terms the manner in which specific cooperation in each specific area envisaged was to be implemented."

This was the first time the court has examined the "development cooperation" articles agreed in the Maastrich Treaty (articles 130uto 130y), with regard to the competency of the EU to enter into agreements with third parties.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: Portugese)
Kingdom of Denmark, United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, Commission of the European Communities, interveners

application for annulment of Council decision 94/578/EC of 18 July 1994 concerning the conclusion of the Cooperation Agreement between the European Community and the Republic of India on Partnership and Development (OJ 1994 L 223, p. 23)
Confirms the validity of the legal basis of the Cooperation Agreement between the European Community and the Republic of India.
